headline: Zoomifier Launches StepIn, Letting Sports Teams Sell Suites and Sponsorships Through AI-Powered 3D Venue Tours
subheadline: Sports organizations can build custom 3D venue experiences in minutes, not weeks, to streamline premium seating and sponsorship sales, with plans starting at $20 per month.
body: Zoomifier today announced the launch of StepIn, an AI-powered 3D experience platform that is designed to change how professional sports teams, college athletic departments and premium entertainment venues sell their spaces.

By letting sales teams capture 360-degree views of a venue and instantly place a prospect’s branding into the experience, StepIn removes friction from the sale of premium seating, corporate hospitality and naming rights.

Traditionally, selling a six-figure luxury suite or stadium sponsorship has meant weeks of in- person site visits or waiting on creative teams to produce custom 3D mockups. StepIn eliminates those bottlenecks. Organizations can capture any section of a venue with a standard pocket-sized 360-degree camera, upload the footage and have an immersive, interactive 3D experience ready in minutes.

The platform introduces StepIn AI, an interactive virtual assistant embedded directly within the 3D venue experience. Prospective buyers can ask questions about premium seating, hospitality options, catering and venue features, with StepIn AI providing immediate, property-specific answers and guiding them to relevant areas of the venue. StepIn is designed to support, not replace, the personal relationships that drive sales. Representatives can share personalized experiences with prospects and key decision-makers, keeping the conversation going well beyond the initial meeting.

“Executives at sports properties are excited by how naturally StepIn showcases high value MMR deals and naming rights opportunities,” said Rupali Saiya, co-founder and Head of Sales at Zoomifier. “Seeing how immersed corporate partners are with 3D StepIn Experiences, I can’t imagine them signing a deal without first stepping into the experience.”

Key StepIn features for sports properties include: ● Instant Brand Personalization: Sales reps can drag and drop a prospective sponsor’s logo and media into signage positions throughout the venue, so brands can see their activation in 3D before they sign. ● Built-in Sales Engagement Tracking: Teams receive real-time analytics showing which decision-makers opened the 3D link, which premium lounges or suites they explored and how long they stayed. ● Live Guided Video Tours: Account executives can lead clients through multiple areas of a venue live using built-in videoconferencing tools, eliminating travel delays and accelerating deal cycles. ● Low Cost of Entry: Unlike expensive, agency-built virtual tours, StepIn requires no specialized photography skills and starts at $20 per month, with a 30-day free trial.

“It’s remarkable how quickly sports teams are going from experiencing StepIn for the first time to delivering a customized StepIn Experience,” said Sameer Saiya, co-founder and Head of Operations at Zoomifier. “We are amazed watching sales teams immediately come up with creative ways to showcase their assets and engage corporate partners in ways they couldn’t before. StepIn has made the sales experience easier and fun.”
StepIn is integrated with the Zoomifier customer engagement platform. To start a free 30-day trial or see the platform in action, visit www.zoomifier.com/stepin.

About Zoomifier
Zoomifier is a sales enablement and customer engagement technology company whose
software solutions help businesses engage buyers and shorten sales cycles with interactive
digital experiences. Its newest product, StepIn, uses AI and 360-degree media to turn real
estate, hospitality and sports venue spaces into interactive sales tools. Zoomifier is
headquartered in San Francisco with presence in Europe and Asia. Its clients include
professional sports leagues and teams, collegiate athletic programs and leading multimedia
rights holders and sports facilities development companies.
